Super Eagles forward, Tolu Arokodare, has said that Nigeria is his life, describing representing the country as a deeply personal responsibility after scoring his first international brace in the 3-1 win over Tanzania. Arokodare scored twice as a substitute in the 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifier at the Godswill Akpabio International Stadium, Uyo, on Friday, November 13. Nigeria had gone 1-0 up through Alhassan Yusuf in the second minute, before Alphonce Msanga levelled in the 32nd. He came on at half-time and restored the lead in the 52nd minute, finishing Wilfred Ndidi’s assist. He completed the brace eight minutes later, after Moses Usor set him up. The goals ended his wait for a goal for the national team. The 25-year-old arrived in camp in impressive form for Ajax, with 13 goals and four assists in 17 appearances in all competitions, including a goal against FC Twente and two against FC Midtjylland. Speaking to Dangolo Way, Arokodare said doing his job was his biggest motivation. My job is to play football, and I enjoy playing football. I had to do my job whenever I am called upon for my club or my country. Whenever I am on the pitch, I have a job to do, and that is my motivation,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Nigeria is my life, so it means everything to me.” He said goals were not his only measure of a good performance. “I try to make myself, my team and the fans happy by scoring goals or helping the team in whatever way I can,” he added. Nigeria face Tanzania again in Zanzibar on Tuesday, November 17, and Arokodare will look to keep his scoring run going.
